topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: It frames the lecture topic, difficulty, and context before the main immunological material begins.

topics.label: Core principles and components of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the foundational concepts, nomenclature rules, and the central role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the mechanisms by which upstream recognition pathways converge to trigger complement activation on pathogen surfaces.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the downstream processes through which activated complement destroys pathogens and drives inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the regulatory mechanisms that prevent complement from attacking and destroying healthy host tissue.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It details the distinct disease presentations and clinical vulnerabilities caused by deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the strategies and molecular mechanisms used by pathogens to resist and evade complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic preview
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
